_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::shell#0. The rule (Kirchhoff-Love needs C1, hence NURBS) holds; the names in the entry did not. On the upstream shell_kl_nurbs deck, which runs as shipped: 'SHELL_KL_NURBS' — the spelling the entry recommended — raises "Unknown type 'SHELL_KL_NURBS' of finite element" from core/comm/src/4C_comm_parobjectfactory.cpp; there is no DKT element at all ("Unknown type 'DKT' of finite element"); the literal 'SHELL KIRCHHOFF QUAD4' spelling is read as element type SHELL with cell type KIRCHHOFF and dies on 'Unknown celltype KIRCHHOFF'; and pairing the CORRECT type name with QUAD4 makes the element type itself unknown rather than reporting a cell-type mismatch, with the offending cell type never echoed (QUAD4_DIAGNOSTIC_NAMES_THE_CELL=0) — which sends a reader looking for a misspelt element name when the element name was right. The working combination is SHELL_KIRCHHOFF_LOVE_NURBS on NURBS9 with MAT_Kirchhoff_Love_shell. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: write the element's real name in the shortname arm. Its 'Unknown type' line vanishes and EXIT_SHORTNAME becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the second pathology: stop asking for a DKT element that does not exist. Its 'Unknown type' line vanishes and EXIT_DKT becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the third pathology: keep the correct cell type. The 'Unknown type SHELL_KIRCHHOFF_LOVE_NURBS' line vanishes and EXIT_QUAD4 becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
